title: Timeouts bound waiting
summary: A timeout sets a limit on waiting. The caller must choose a useful response when that limit passes.
introduction: A timeout sets a limit on waiting. The caller must choose a useful response when that limit passes. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A timeout sets a limit on waiting. The caller must choose a useful response when that limit passes.

blocks.code:
Request begins at 0 ms
Timeout limit: 800 ms
No reply at 800 ms -> show a retry message
blocks.title: Timeouts bound waiting

blocks.text: The caller stops waiting after the limit. The remote work might still be running.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Choose a clear user message for a timed-out search.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: A timeout does not cancel all work in another service automatically.
For more detail later, use this [Microservices further reading](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/microservices/).

seo.title: Microservices: Timeouts bound waiting
seo.description: Learn about timeouts bound waiting in Microservices. Follow a small example, understand the result, and practise with a clear question.
